item.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
item.description: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
item.content: Before returning any Decimal money value, check ledgerly/money.py for a round_money (or similar) helper and wrap the final result with it. Python's round() and default quantize() use banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Read the money module before implementing money logic
item.description: Inspect ledgerly/money.py early to discover ZERO, to_money, and round_money conventions used across the codebase.
item.content: Existing functions like line_total and invoice_total show the pattern: convert inputs with to_money, accumulate with ZERO as the sum start, and round the final result with round_money. Mirror that pattern for any new money-returning function.

item.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly
item.description: Guard against division by zero and return the project's ZERO constant for empty inputs.
item.content: When computing an average over a collection, sum the denominator first and return ZERO (the money module's zero constant) if it is zero, rather than dividing and risking ZeroDivisionError or returning a plain int 0.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for validation
item.description: Validate monetary inputs by converting through the module's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than ad-hoc checks.
item.content: When a codebase has money utilities like to_money and round_money, use them to normalize and compare against ZERO instead of writing custom Decimal parsing. This keeps rounding and type coercion consistent with the rest of the module.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer types
item.description: In Python, isinstance(True, int) is True, so explicitly reject bool before checking int for quantity fields.
item.content: When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool)` first and reject it, then check `isinstance(x, int)`. Otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and corrupt data.

item.title: Match existing error codes and state checks
item.description: Mirror the error codes and status-guard patterns already used by sibling functions in the same module.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, read neighboring functions (e.g. issue_invoice) to copy their BillingError codes and status-check style. Consistency with existing conventions is what hidden tests typically assert.

item.title: Reuse existing helpers for datetime normalization and errors
item.description: When implementing a new function in a module, check sibling modules for established helpers like ensure_utc and BillingError and reuse them for consistency.
item.content: Before writing validation logic, grep the package for existing utilities (e.g., ensure_utc, BillingError) and mirror the patterns used in analogous functions like current_period. This keeps error codes and timezone handling consistent with the rest of the codebase.

item.title: Compute strictly-after occurrences with floor division plus one
item.description: For periodic events from a start time, the first occurrence strictly after a timestamp is start + ((after - start) // length + 1) * length.
item.content: Use integer floor division on timedeltas to find the index of the period containing `after`, then add one to get the strictly-next boundary. Handle the before-start case separately by returning start + length, since the start itself is not a renewal.

item.title: Validate period_days defensively against bool and non-positive values
item.description: Guard against bool (subclass of int) and non-positive period_days by raising the domain error rather than letting timedelta misbehave.
item.content: Check `not isinstance(x, bool) and isinstance(x, int) and x > 0` before constructing timedelta; otherwise raise BillingError with a machine-readable code. This prevents silent zero/negative periods and bool coercion bugs.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` on every operation that changes a payment/credit/invoice balance. Scan `audit.events(<event_type>)` for a matching key and return the original record immediately; only then validate state. Include the key in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Enforce approval threshold for large refunds/credits
item.description: Support-initiated refunds or credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03.
item.content: Accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None`. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when `approved_by` is missing. Callers without approval needs keep working unchanged.

item.title: Serialize Decimal amounts as float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values, so audit entries must write amounts as `float(amount)`.
item.content: When recording audit events for money operations, convert Decimal amounts with `float(amount)` before passing them to `audit.record`. Keep internal arithmetic in Decimal via `round_money`; only the audit payload uses float.

item.title: Explore repo conventions before implementing
item.description: Reading money.py, errors.py, and sibling modules first revealed the project's Decimal-based money helpers and error type, enabling a correct first-attempt implementation.
item.content: Before writing new functions, inspect the target module's neighbors and shared utilities (money, errors, models). Mirror existing helper functions like to_money/round_money and the project's BillingError(code, message) pattern instead of inventing new conventions.

item.title: Use Decimal for money math, never float
item.description: The repo's to_money rejects floats and round_money applies ROUND_HALF_UP; using Decimal throughout avoids precision and rounding bugs.
item.content: Convert inputs via to_money, perform arithmetic with Decimal (e.g. amount * rate / Decimal('100')), and round the final result with round_money. This matches the repository's rounding policy and passes hidden tests expecting cent-accurate results.

item.title: Validate ranges with inclusive bounds and domain errors
item.description: Checking rate < 0 or rate > 100 correctly enforces the inclusive 0–100 constraint and raises the project's BillingError with a descriptive code.
item.content: For range constraints, use strict comparisons on both ends (x < min or x > max) to keep bounds inclusive. Raise the project's domain exception (BillingError) with a short machine-readable code rather than a generic ValueError.

item.title: Check idempotency key before state validation
item.description: When adding an operation that moves money, look up the idempotency key in audit events first and return the original result before validating state or applying changes.
item.content: Team convention (INC-204): every money-moving or balance-changing function must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event_type>)` for a matching key first; if found, return the original record unchanged. Only then validate state and mutate. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Cast Decimal amounts to float in audit entries
item.description: Audit entries must store amounts as float(amount) because the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
item.content: When calling `audit.record(...)`, pass `amount=float(payment.amount)` rather than the raw Decimal. This is a repo-wide convention; violating it breaks downstream JSON import even if local tests pass.

item.title: Inspect sibling modules for conventions before implementing
item.description: Before writing a new function, read adjacent modules (audit, clock, errors, other payment/invoice ops) to discover implicit conventions like idempotency and serialization rules.
item.content: The first attempt failed because it only read the target file and tests, missing the idempotency and float conventions. Grep for `idempotency_key` and `audit.record` across the repo to surface team-wide patterns before coding.
